findings.where: Hero, the handwritten red 'write to me' note in the left margin (desktop); the tile has no button specimen anywhere
findings.fault: The page's one action, getting in touch with Mark, is shown only as a small scribble set apart in the margin, about 130 px wide. Its underline is drawn as the pen stroke, so it reads as an annotation, not a control. The headline, the clipped photo and the aqueduct drawing all carry far more weight, so the order of visual weight is the reverse of the order of tasks. The tile also gives no button look at all (no fill, no edge, no ladder), so the next round has no form for the action. On the phone the note moves into the text column and reads more clearly, but it still has no button form.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has decided to contact Mark scans the first screen for a contact button and finds none. They may take the margin note for decoration and miss it, then fall back on the small 'Contact' item in the nav. Mark would object because getting in touch is the page's whole job.

findings.where: Article specimen, the attached-document row 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge · Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Only the title is a link. Bold weight is all that marks it, and the same bold ballpoint is used for static labels (palette names, table headings). The rules above and below run across the whole row, so they read as table lines rather than a link underline. The word 'PDF', the cue a reader looks for, sits in the static half of the row, where a click does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A reader who wants the lecture PDF clicks 'PDF' or the date and gets nothing, or does not see the title as a link at all. Angélique will repeat this row for every PDF Mark posts, so the hidden link would be on every article page.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the 'Replay the note' button at the foot of the box (desktop)
findings.fault: The button replays the margin note, which sits about two screens above it at the top of the page. On desktop, pressing it shows no visible change, so it looks like a dead action. It is also styled as an underlined link although it acts in place, so it uses the link's reserved underline.
findings.who_objects: Mark or the founder, judging the motion sketch from the tile: they press Replay, see nothing happen and assume it is broken. They would have to scroll back up to watch an animation that has already finished.

findings.where: The handwriting face across the page: the red 'write to me' action, the blue pull quote in the article specimen, and the 'written, steady, by hand' heading in the motion sketch
findings.fault: The handwriting is the only thing that marks the page's one action, yet the same face also sets a static quote and a static heading. Only colour and the pen underline tell them apart, so the handwritten look stands for two functions: act here, and read Mark's voice.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who learns on the homepage that Mark's handwriting means 'write to me' meets the handwritten quote on an article page and tries to click it, or the reverse. Once handwriting means 'aside', they skip the call to action.
